    {
      "model_finding_id": "F1",
      "proposition": "Prioritise GBP7 and GBP10 as competing candidates for real-behaviour testing. Their valid-case gross price-times-intent proxies are GBP3.633 and GBP3.363 per hypothetical household-month, compared with GBP2.673 at GBP4 and GBP2.576 at GBP13. Both middle prices exceed both endpoints under the declared adjusted tests; GBP7's numerical lead over GBP10 does not establish superiority.",
      "evidence_refs": ["#/analysis_claims/2/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Research recommendation supported by four Holm-adjusted gross-proxy contrasts; comparison between shortlisted prices unresolved",
      "qualification": "Valid n at GBP4/7/10/13 is 704/682/655/633. GBP7 minus GBP10 is GBP0.270, unadjusted pointwise 95% CI −0.189 to 0.728, Holm p=0.498. Adjusted p values for the four middle-price versus endpoint contrasts range from 7.47e-9 to 0.01393. These mechanical indices are not revenue forecasts; nonsignificance does not establish equivalence or an optimum.",
      "topic_cluster": "price_test_priority"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F5",
      "proposition": "Keep both candidates because the numerical contribution leader depends on assumed cost and missing-response scoring. At costs GBP0.50, GBP2 and GBP3, valid-case contribution proxies are respectively GBP3.373, GBP2.595 and GBP2.076 for GBP7, versus GBP3.195, GBP2.690 and GBP2.354 for GBP10. At the GBP2 base cost, conservative all-assigned proxies are nearly identical: GBP2.362 and GBP2.358.",
      "evidence_refs": ["#/analysis_claims/3/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Scenario-dependent numerical rankings; no adjusted evidence of superiority between GBP7 and GBP10",
      "qualification": "Valid n is 682 at GBP7 and 655 at GBP10; each assigned base is 750. GBP7-minus-GBP10 differences across the three costs are GBP0.178, −0.096 and −0.278, with joint-family Holm p=1, 1 and 0.418. At base cost, the unadjusted pointwise difference CI is −0.449 to 0.258; both middle prices exceed GBP4 after adjustment, but neither is shown to exceed GBP13 (p=0.263 and 0.208). Costs are hypothetical per proxy-positive subscriber-month. These are contribution indices, not profits; near-identical estimates do not prove equivalence.",
      "topic_cluster": "cost_sensitivity"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F2",
      "proposition": "GBP4 provides the strongest stated-interest benchmark, showing the interest sacrificed at higher prices. Positive intent falls across GBP4/7/10/13 from 66.84% to 51.90%, 33.63% and 19.82%. The full distribution also shifts: definitely-would-not rises from 10.98% to 55.81% between endpoints, while definitely-would falls from 42.88% to 7.08%.",
      "evidence_refs": ["#/analysis_claims/1/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "All six positive-intent differences supported after prespecified Holm adjustment; individual category shifts descriptive",
      "qualification": "Valid n=704/682/655/633 in ascending price order. GBP7 exceeds GBP10 by 18.27 percentage points, unadjusted pointwise 95% CI 12.90–23.63; all six P1 adjusted p<0.000001. Valid-case comparisons condition on post-assignment observation and do not establish purchases or full-sample causal effects.",
      "topic_cluster": "stated_interest"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F3",
      "proposition": "Increasing missing intent qualifies the price comparison. Missing responses account for 5.58%, 8.99%, 12.35% and 15.46% of assigned weight across GBP4/7/10/13. Conservative recorded-positive yields preserve the descending order at 63.11%, 47.23%, 29.48% and 16.75%, but possible completions of missing responses need not preserve every comparison.",
      "evidence_refs": ["#/analysis_claims/0/values/assigned_bases", "#/analysis_claims/1/values"],
      "importance": "primary",
      "claim_strength": "Descriptive missingness pattern and Holm-adjusted all-assigned recorded-positive comparisons",
      "qualification": "Each arm contains 750 assigned households; all six P2 adjusted p<0.000001. Don't-know shares increase from 2.37% to 8.95%; module exits are not monotonic. Logical completion ranges are 63.11–68.69%, 47.23–56.22%, 29.48–41.83% and 16.75–32.22%; GBP10 and GBP13 overlap. These ranges exclude sampling uncertainty and are neither confidence intervals nor actual-demand bounds. Baseline weights do not correct missingness; conservative scoring does not turn missing responses into observed rejection.",
      "topic_cluster": "response_uncertainty"
    },
    {
      "model_finding_id": "F6",
      "proposition": "Include time-pressed families as a prespecified audience in behavioural testing. Their positive stated intent is 62.74% versus 47.10% among other known-status households at GBP7, and 46.23% versus 28.26% at GBP10.",
      "evidence_refs": ["#/analysis_claims/4/values"],
      "importance": "secondary",
